svg.aria-label: Diagram: the new EC2 Auto Scaling launchBeforeTerminate account setting is a fallback rather than an override. It applies to groups that do not define an instance maintenance policy or set instance refresh preferences, so groups configured deliberately keep their own behaviour. Each account setting also applies to the entire account within a single AWS Region, so it must be configured in every Region where it should take effect. The per-group instance maintenance policy remains the richer control, expressing minimum and maximum healthy percentages rather than a single enabled or disabled value, and a larger range increases the number of instances replaced at the same time.
svg.title: An account setting that yields to every group with an opinion
svg.text: An account-level default that the configured groups ignore.
EC2 Auto Scaling — launchBeforeTerminate, set once instead of group by group.
What it does, and it is the behaviour most people want
“Auto Scaling launches a replacement instance and waits for it to pass health checks before terminating
the instance it replaces” — on instance refreshes, rebalancing, health checks and maximum-instance-lifetime.
PutAccountSetting · DescribeAccountSettings · all Regions, no additional cost
QUALIFICATION 1 — it is a fallback
“applies to groups that don’t define an instance

text.tspan: maintenance policy or set instance refresh

svg.text: preferences”
The groups configured deliberately are usually the
production ones. It lands on the rest.
QUALIFICATION 2 — it is per Region
“Each account setting applies to your entire
account within a single AWS Region.”
“Configure a setting in every Region where you
want it to take effect.”
So: account baseline, not a click.
The per-group control stays the richer one, which is why the account setting defers to it
ACCOUNT SETTING enabled | disabled → a switch
MAINTENANCE POLICY minimum and maximum healthy percentage → a range you control
“A larger range increases the number of instances that can be replaced at the same time.”
Both express the same intent: launch first, wait until ready, then terminate.
Free is not the same as costless.
The feature is “available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost”. Launching before terminating still means briefly
running more instances than desired capacity, and that time bills like any other. Neither page quantifies it, because
it depends on health check duration and how many instances replace at once.
Before enabling: list the groups that already define a policy or refresh preferences. Those are the ones it will not
touch, and knowing which they are is the difference between a default and an assumption.
